## Summary

Acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) by acetylation of salicylic acid, the
product of OSDB-0001, with acetic anhydride and a phosphoric acid
catalyst. This is sample data: the quantities follow the textbook method
but are not experimentally verified.

## Reagents

| Reagent | CAS | MW (g/mol) | Amount | mmol | Equiv |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Salicylic acid | 69-72-7 | 138.12 | 2.76 g | 20.0 | 1.0 |
| Acetic anhydride | 108-24-7 | 102.09 | 6.13 g (5.67 mL) | 60.0 | 3.0 |
| Phosphoric acid, 85 % | 7664-38-2 | 97.99 | 5 drops | cat. | cat. |

## Procedure

1. Place the dry salicylic acid (2.76 g, 20.0 mmol) in a 100 mL conical
   flask.
2. In a fume hood, add the acetic anhydride (6.13 g, 5.67 mL, 60.0 mmol)
   and then 5 drops of 85 % phosphoric acid, and swirl to mix.
3. Heat the flask on a water bath at 70 to 80 °C for 15 minutes, swirling
   from time to time, until all the solid has dissolved.
4. Remove the flask from the bath and, while it is still warm, add water
   (2 mL) dropwise to destroy the excess acetic anhydride. The reaction
   is vigorous and gives off hot acetic acid vapour.
5. Add cold water (40 mL) and cool the flask in an ice bath until
   crystallisation is complete. Scratch the inside of the flask with a
   glass rod if no crystals form.

## Workup and Purification

Collect the crude product by suction filtration and wash it with two
portions of ice-cold water (5 mL each). Recrystallise it from a small
volume of hot ethanol diluted with warm water, cool in ice, filter, and
dry the crystals in air. Expected yield 2.70 g (15.0 mmol, 75 %).

## Characterization

Colourless needles, mp 134 to 136 °C (literature 135 °C). A solution in
ethanol gives no violet colour with a drop of iron(III) chloride solution,
showing that no salicylic acid remains.

## Notes

1. The salicylic acid must be dry: water consumes acetic anhydride.
2. Heat the product gently when recrystallising; prolonged boiling in
   water hydrolyses it back to salicylic acid.

## Hazards and Waste Disposal

Acetic anhydride is flammable, causes severe burns and is harmful if
inhaled; handle it in a fume hood with gloves and eye protection.
Phosphoric acid causes burns. Salicylic acid causes serious eye damage,
and both it and the product are harmful if swallowed. Collect the
acidic filtrates, neutralise them, and dispose of them as aqueous waste.

1. Furniss, B. S.; Hannaford, A. J.; Smith, P. W. G.; Tatchell, A. R.
